prompt: Which is the correct order of the classical TTS pipeline?
options: vocoder, acoustic model, text frontend
acoustic model, text frontend, vocoder
text frontend, acoustic model (to mel), vocoder
text frontend, vocoder, acoustic model
explanation: Text is normalised and phonemised, the acoustic model predicts a mel spectrogram, the vocoder converts it to a waveform.

prompt: A length regulator expands 4 phonemes with durations (2, 3, 1, 2). How many mel frames result?
Why can a mel spectrogram not be inverted exactly, even in principle?
options: mel filters are linear, so inversion is trivial
it discards phase and, through the filters, fine frequency detail
it is stored with too few bits
it uses the wrong window
explanation: Both the phase and the resolution inside each mel band are lost; many waveforms share the same mel picture.

prompt: The least-squares inverse STFT with analysis window $w$ is computed by...
options: inverse FFT of each frame, windowing again, overlap-add, division by the summed $w^2$
inverse FFT followed by averaging adjacent frames without a window
keeping only the first frame
multiplying by the pseudo-inverse of the mel filterbank
explanation: Setting the derivative of $\sum_t\|w\odot x_t-y_t\|^2$ to zero gives $x[m]=\sum_tw\,y_t/\sum_tw^2$.

options: adding noise to the magnitude and renormalising
training a neural network for one step
halving the hop size
inverse STFT, STFT, then keeping the new phase and restoring the target magnitude
explanation: Alternate projection onto consistent spectrograms (ISTFT then STFT) and onto spectrograms with the prescribed magnitude.

prompt: After many Griffin-Lim iterations the reconstructed waveform differs from the original by a large RMS error although the spectral convergence is small. Why is this not a bug?
options: the sampling rate was wrong
only the magnitude was specified; many waveforms (e.g. $x$ and $-x$) share it
the window was not Hann
the inverse STFT is inexact
explanation: Phase retrieval from magnitude is not unique, so compare magnitudes (spectral convergence), not samples.

prompt: Ten listeners give a MOS with sample mean 3.8 and sample standard deviation 0.9. What is the half-width of the 95% normal-approximation confidence interval (use 1.96)? Round to two decimals.
A neural codec runs at 75 frames/s with 8 codebooks of 1024 entries. What is the bitrate in bits per second?
Which statement about safeguards against voice-cloning misuse is the most accurate?
options: a watermark makes misuse impossible
detectors reach a fixed accuracy on any new generator
consent, provenance marks, detection and policy are complementary and each has limits
a high SECS value proves the speaker consented
explanation: None of the controls is sufficient alone: watermarks can be removed or absent, detectors age against new generators, SECS measures similarity and not permission.
